summary: An application's navigation as a column: pinned header and footer that take any component, a scrolling body of titled, collapsible sections, and nested items that expand.
useWhen: an app has more destinations than fit in a header — workspaces, projects, saved views
the navigation is hierarchical and users need to see where they are inside it
rows need their own actions — create inside this space, rename, favourite

useInstead.when: there are five or fewer top-level destinations and no hierarchy
useInstead.why: a sidebar spends a column of width on what a header row carries in its height

useInstead.when: the hierarchy describes the current page's position rather than offering destinations
sections of content collapse, not destinations
useInstead.why: Accordion's headings belong to the document outline; a sidebar is a navigation landmark

composition.note: Items always go inside a section, because a section renders the list. Anything that is not an item — a Divider, a promotional Alert — goes directly in Sidebar between sections, or in `header` / `footer`. On narrow screens, put the Sidebar inside a Drawer; it does not collapse itself.
composition.example: <Sidebar label="Workspace" header={<WorkspaceMenu />} footer={<Button>Invite</Button>}><SidebarSection><SidebarItem label="Home" href="/" isCurrent /></SidebarSection><Divider /><SidebarSection title="Spaces" isCollapsible><SidebarItem label="Team Space" href="/team"><SidebarItem label="Projects" href="/team/projects" /></SidebarItem></SidebarSection></Sidebar>

header.note: pinned above the scroll — a workspace switcher, search, icon Buttons

footer.note: pinned below the scroll — Invite, Help, a trial notice in an Alert

children.note: and Divider or other non-item content between sections

requires: `label` — the accessible name of the navigation landmark. Pages with a sidebar usually have a second nav, and two unnamed ones cannot be told apart
guarantees: only the body scrolls; the header and footer stay reachable at any scroll position
notes: it is disclosure navigation, not a treeview: everything is reachable with Tab, and rows can hold buttons. The tree role forbids interactive content inside items and would have ruled out row actions

antiPatterns.dont: role="tree" on a sidebar with row actions
antiPatterns.why: a treeview item cannot contain buttons, and its arrow-key model hides every action from Tab

antiPatterns.dont: a SidebarItem placed directly in Sidebar, outside a section
antiPatterns.why: the item renders an <li>, which is only valid inside the list a section provides

antiPatterns.dont: a sidebar that is only ever a hamburger menu on desktop
antiPatterns.why: hierarchical navigation that is hidden by default is navigation nobody uses; hide it only where the width forces it
